purpose: Test whether adding the fixed-state Sinocirsium tips from the same Chang 2026 East Asian time-tree context constrains flower-colour transition rate enough to identify the Arenicola ancestor.

excluded_polymorphic_tip.reason: Direct W/BP polymorphism is source-backed; do not collapse to a fixed species-level state.

sinocirsium_shallow_age_sensitivity.reason: Chang 2026 reports several shallow Taiwanese C. japonicum-complex nodes spanning approximately 0.08-0.44 Mya but the exact machine-readable node ages are unavailable. These are nuisance sensitivities, not extracted node ages.

sources.use: East Asian subsection topology; 1.30, 1.02, 0.93, 0.79 and 0.44 Mya medians; Sinocirsium topology; fixed flower-colour states.
Taiwanese Nipponocirsium sensitivity scaffold: pengii basal and 0.47/0.35 Mya medians, with alternative basal resolutions retained as sensitivity.

claim_boundary: This is a hybrid published-node-age sensitivity scaffold, not an extracted Chang BEAST/ASTRAL tree. The Sinocirsium shallow ages are nuisance grids because the exact time-tree file is unavailable. It diagnoses rate identifiability only; it is not a final posterior ASR or stochastic map.
